population_label: counted cache lookups in the measured windows (hits + misses) on the cached arm
not_shown: A steady-state WARM window. Every concurrency level runs an uncounted warmup first, so this is not a cold-start hit rate and must never be read as one. The sequence's own ceiling for a perfect cache is 0.9445.

population_label: offered-rate levels on the uncached arm's open-loop ladder, stepped 2,000 rps
not_shown: A QUANTISED LOWER BOUND, not the capacity. The ladder steps 2,000 rps, so all this establishes is that the arm held its highest passing level and failed at the next one: the true capacity lies in [bracket_low, bracket_high). A ratio formed from this figure and its cached counterpart would net two lower bounds and is refused for that reason.

population_label: one open-loop ladder level on the uncached arm, at the highest offered rate both arms held
not_shown: ONE reading. The ladder runs each level once, so this figure's population is 1 and it carries no interval. The rate is chosen as the highest both arms held, because a tail pair read at a rate one arm cannot serve compares a working system against a collapsed one.

population_label: one open-loop ladder level on the cached arm, at the highest offered rate both arms held
not_shown: ONE reading. The ladder runs each level once, so this figure's population is 1 and it carries no interval. The rate is chosen as the highest both arms held, because a tail pair read at a rate one arm cannot serve compares a working system against a collapsed one.

population_label: independent replicates at 6,000 rps offered on the uncached arm, run interleaved by round
not_shown: Three replicates on one host on one day. The record this supersedes reports three consecutive failures at this identical rate, so this figure is evidence that the earlier instability came from uncontrolled load on the same machine and is not proof of it.

population_label: independent replicates at 8,000 rps offered on the cached arm, run interleaved by round
not_shown: Three replicates at the highest rate this arm was replicated at. It is NOT this arm's capacity: the ladder held to 12,000 rps, and 8,000 is where the boundary sweep was run.

population_label: concurrency levels on the uncached arm's closed-loop sweep
not_shown: CLOSED loop. Every virtual user waits for its own response, so the offered rate follows the service's speed and the p99 ceiling does no work. This is the coordinated-omission shape the open-loop ladder exists to replace, kept because the two methods disagreeing would itself be a finding.

population_label: do-nothing probe levels the generator's ceiling is the maximum over
not_shown: The generator's own ceiling on an endpoint that does nothing. It prices every other figure here: a throughput number within reach of this one is measuring the tool. It is the MAXIMUM over three probe levels, not a mean, because the ceiling is what the tool can do at its best.
